Pfizer COVID-19 Vaccine Trial

Source: R/data.R
pfizer.Rd

Data from the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine trial (Polack et al., 2020), a large-scale randomized trial studying vaccine efficacy against symptomatic COVID-19. 40,137 participants were randomized to vaccine or placebo.

Usage

pfizer

Format

A data frame with 1 row and 4 variables:

y0

Number of COVID-19 cases in the placebo group (169).

N0

Number of subjects in the placebo group (20,172).

y1

Number of COVID-19 cases in the vaccine group (9).

N1

Number of subjects in the vaccine group (19,965).

References

Polack, F.P., Thomas, S.J., Kitchin, N. et al. (2020). Safety and Efficacy of the BNT162b2 mRNA Covid-19 Vaccine. New England Journal of Medicine, 383(27), 2603--2615.

Irons, N.J. and Cinelli, C. (2025). Causally Sound Priors for Binary Experiments. Bayesian Analysis. doi:10.1214/25-BA1506

Examples

data(pfizer)
brease(pfizer$y0, pfizer$y1, pfizer$N0, pfizer$N1)
#> Bayesian Analysis of Binary Experiment
#> Method: BREASE 
#> 
#> Data:
#>   Control:   y0 = 169, N0 = 20172 (rate = 0.0084)
#>   Treatment: y1 = 9, N1 = 19965 (rate = 0.0005)
#> 
#> Prior:
#>   theta0 ~ Beta(1.00, 1.00)  [mu0 = 0.50, n0 = 2.0]
#>   eta_e  ~ Beta(0.30, 0.70)  [mue = 0.30, ne = 1.0]
#>   eta_s  ~ Beta(0.30, 0.70)  [mus = 0.30, ns = 1.0]
#> 
#> Posterior Summaries:
#>   Baseline Risk (theta0)        Mean: 0.00839  [0.00718, 0.00969]
#>   Treatment Risk (theta1)       Mean: 0.000502  [0.00024, 0.000858]
#>   Risk Ratio (RR)               Mean: 0.0602  [0.0283, 0.105]
#>   Efficacy Fraction (EF)        Mean: 0.94  [0.895, 0.972]
#>   Odds Ratio (OR)               Mean: 0.0597  [0.028, 0.104]
#>   Risk Difference (RD)          Mean: -0.00789  [-0.00921, -0.00663]
#> 
#> Bayes Factor (BF10): 4.32e+35
#> Bayes Factor (BF01): 2.32e-36
